test_title: PYST 4: SSC Stenographer - English (Held On:13 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Shops are not allowed / to remain open / after 8:00 pm / from the lockdown.
solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 4"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The erroneous part is the use of **"from the lockdown"**.
 
• The phrase** "from the lockdown"** implies that the restriction on shops remaining open starts at the exact moment of the lockdown.
 
• So, the error lies in using **"from"** which is used to convey a starting point at the time of the lockdown but it is wrong.
 
 
• **Example**: *Raj has been living in London since 2003.*
 
 
 
• Hence, it should be replaced with **"since".**

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 4"**.

**Correct Sentence**: "Shops are not allowed to remain open after 8:00 pm **since__** the lockdown."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **"Since"** and **"for"** are both prepositions used to indicate duration, but they are used in different contexts:

 
 
• **"Since"** is used to specify a starting point in time. It indicates when an action or state began.

 
 
• **Example**: *She has been studying English since 2015.*
 
 
 
• **"For" **is used to indicate a duration of time. It specifies the length of time during which an action or state occurred.
 
 
• **Example**: *She studied English for three years.*
